tools.name: Deku
tools.readmeHtml:
Deku

Describe a development environment once in deku.toml; Deku plants it on any machine — runtimes, services, env vars, seeded databases.

Usage

deku sprout        # build the environment described by deku.toml
deku shell         # drop into it
deku prune         # tear it down, keep the cache

Status

Beta. The deku.toml format is still moving; pin a version if you depend on it.

tools.name: Korok
tools.readmeHtml:
Korok

Korok walks a repository and surfaces the things you forgot were there: stale TODOs, orphaned fixtures, dead feature flags, files no import graph reaches.

Usage

korok scan .
korok scan --only=dead-code --format=json
korok seeds        # everything Korok found, grouped

Why

Grep tells you where a string is. Korok tells you what nothing points at.
